text:
Predicates:
Good(x) ::: x is a good guy.
Win(x) ::: x wins.
HeroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Lose(x) ::: x loses.
AppearIn(x, y) ::: x appears in movie y.
Premises:
∀x (HeroMovie(x) → Win(x)) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
HeroMovie(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x (Good(x) ↔ Fight(x, badGuy)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ((HeroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y)) → Good(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
Win(x) → Lose(fightingPartner(x)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀x ((HeroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y)) → AppearIn(y, x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
Lose(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
